scopeNotes: All three map IDs have Newfoundland geometry. Shared narrative association does not verify the polygons or the earliest 800 CE label as a securely dated Beothuk identity.
The 1000 to 1500 phase is approximate archaeological context. BP dates in older publications are not converted by subtracting them from the current year.
Museum acquisition and excavation are not conflated. Boyd’s Cove houses, hearths and food remains are archaeological finds; Shanawdithit’s drawings are testimony.
The Innu ceremonial comparison remains an interpretation. No complete Beothuk religious system is reconstructed from a hearth.
Possible survivors are acknowledged without assigning individual ancestry or making genomic claims. A death date is not automatically the date every community ended.
The independent narrative, geometry and depth reviews remain pending. No modern state or tribe is assigned as a successor merely because of geography.
